eligibility_rule: excluded_publication_type when the publication type names a protocol, correction/erratum, editorial or retraction notice/retracted publication, or (fallback) the title carries an explicit cue ('study protocol', 'Protocol for a ... trial', 'Correction:', 'Editorial:', 'Retraction:'); excluded rows keep their other labels but never enter a review queue
false_negative_audit: criterion 5 of doc 14 is not satisfied by this machine run; a deterministic audit sample with blank human columns is in data/research/v3_gap_search/
hash_basis: sha256 over the exact bytes written (UTF-8, LF line endings); these are the bytes git stores, and data/research/.gitattributes keeps them LF on checkout
limitations: Relevance signals are heuristic lexical clues from title only; false positives and false negatives are expected.
High priority is not evidence quality, human approval, clinical safety or permission for model training.
The underlying 7580 candidates have strong 2025–2026 recency bias.
Only licensed full-text sources may later enter a content-based RAG index, after human appraisal.
Publication-type eligibility relies on Europe PMC pubType tokens and explicit title cues; a protocol or notice without either cue stays eligible, and an excluded row is never deleted from the index.
screening_unit: publication title only (plus year/identifiers for queue)

supersedes.reason: v1.0 hashed CRLF bytes (csv default line ending) while git stores LF, so the committed index and worksheet never matched their manifest hashes (audit P1); v1.0 also let 3 correction notices and 8 protocols into the 400 queue (audit P5)
